newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council had kept the German discount and Lombard rates steady after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank also said it had fixed its main money market rate at three percent for the next two weeks.
Economists had not expected any change in credit policy at the meeting, particularly after several Bundesbank council members have said recently they saw no need to change credit costs any time soon.
Even news that German unemployment surged to a record level in January was judged by analysts as unlikely to prompt the tough Bundesbank into a policy move.

Economists are divided as to whether the Bundesbank will lower interest rates again in this easing cycle. Some believe the next move will be a tightening, but they say this is unlikely to take place until the year-end at the earliest.
